ANTH 101.description: An exploration of human origins, human evolution, human prehistory, and cultural existence from its less complex forms to early civilizations. An introduction to the concepts, methods, and data of physical, biological, and archaeological anthropology.
ANTH 101.subject: ANTH
ANTH 101.title: Primates, People, and Prehistory

ANTH 102.description: An exploration and comparison of selected contemporary cultures, including their languages. An introduction to the concepts, methods, and data of socio-cultural anthropology and anthropological linguistics.
ANTH 102.subject: ANTH
ANTH 102.title: Understanding Other Cultures

ANTH 161.description: An introduction to the science of biological anthropology, a sub-field of anthropology that emphasizes a focus on humanity and its origin from a biological perspective, employing laboratory components to complement and reinforce lecture materials.
ANTH 161.subject: ANTH
ANTH 161.title: Human Origins: An Introduction to Biological Anthropology

ANTH 201.description: Introduces research-based learning in anthropology from a four-field perspective. To encourage self-reflective, professional thinking and provide experience and practice in professional skills and applications in anthropology.
ANTH 201.subject: ANTH
ANTH 201.title: Anthropological Inquiry in Undergraduate Research

ANTH 203.description: Human behavior in differing cultural contexts through ethnographic films of social relations in selected societies.
ANTH 203.subject: ANTH
ANTH 203.title: Comparing Cultures Through Film

ANTH 204.description: An overview of how plagues and epidemics have shaped human prehistory and history. How large-scale social transformations have produced forms of human/disease interactions. How infectious disease has been conceptualized at different times and by different cultural groups and treated as a threat to the social order.
ANTH 204.subject: ANTH
ANTH 204.title: Plagues Past and Present

ANTH 206.description: A comparative examination of such topics as ritual, cosmology, revitalization movements, magic, witchcraft, myth, and possession.
ANTH 206.subject: ANTH
ANTH 206.title: Anthropology of Magic and Religion

ANTH 207.description: Anthropological study of gender, with emphasis on cross-cultural investigation of the interaction of biological, cultural, and environmental factors including intersections of race, social class, and sexuality as influences gender behavior.
ANTH 207.subject: ANTH
ANTH 207.title: Gender and Culture

ANTH 208.description: Examine cross-cultural definitions and experiences of globalization and development, through topics including colonial legacies of inequality, migration, land use, economic restructuring, media, consumption, tourism, health, and participatory development.
ANTH 208.subject: ANTH
ANTH 208.title: Anthropology of Globalization and Development

ANTH 209.description: Folk expression as shaped by various cultures; fieldwork methodology and anthropological theory.
ANTH 209.subject: ANTH
ANTH 209.title: Introduction to Folklore

ANTH 210.description: Childhood, maturity, old age, and gender socialization within the family.
ANTH 210.subject: ANTH
ANTH 210.title: Human Life Cycles in Different Cultures

ANTH 211.description: Classroom ethnography, bilingualism, cultural minorities, communication across cultural boundaries. Films, videotapes, and fieldwork in classroom settings.
ANTH 211.subject: ANTH
ANTH 211.title: Learning Across Cultures

ANTH 212.description: Biological and cultural interactions affecting foodways around the world, and associated ethical issues.
ANTH 212.subject: ANTH
ANTH 212.title: Food and Culture

ANTH 213.description: Anthropological overview of the interactions between cultures around the world and the plants that affect them, from cultural, biological, archaeological, and linguistic points of view.
ANTH 213.subject: ANTH
ANTH 213.title: Ethnobotany: Plants and Peoples

ANTH 214.description: Cultures of alcohol production and consumption from ancient times to the present, including relationships among social roles of alcohol, technological innovations, agriculture, and economy in an anthropological perspective.
ANTH 214.subject: ANTH
ANTH 214.title: Drinking in Culture: Anthropology of Alcohol

ANTH 216.description: Violence and peace in current events, cultural practices, historical periods, and everyday experiences. The ethics shaping violence and peace-making strategies. Classroom discussions and lectures analyzing harm and wellbeing. Themes addressing the Values, Ethics, and Social Responsibility (VSR) Carolina Core component, including colonialism, environmental exploitation, bondage, mass extinctions, and racism.
ANTH 216.subject: ANTH
ANTH 216.title: Violence and Peace: Anthropological Perspectives

ANTH 219.description: Survey of key archaeological discoveries from around the world.
ANTH 219.subject: ANTH
ANTH 219.title: Great Discoveries in Archaeology

ANTH 221.description: Forensic methods of Sherlock Holmes within the context of modern forensic science. Aspects of forensic science including history of the discipline, forensic pathology, entomology, print analyses, crime scene analysis, forensic anthropology, early scientific theory, and anthropological theory of Holmes.
ANTH 221.subject: ANTH
ANTH 221.title: Forensics of Sherlock Holmes

ANTH 223.description: Explores the last five centuries of world history, using artifacts and archival sources. Evidence such as probate records, bottles, and geophysical maps are analyzed to discover the age of sites and answers to questions about topics such as colonialism, race, technology, piracy, class, Native Americans, industrialization, slavery, inequality, capitalism, and gender.
ANTH 223.subject: ANTH
ANTH 223.title: Modernity Archaeology and the Recent Past

ANTH 224.description: Historical archaeology and ethnography of the Casimiroid, Ortoiroid, Saladoid, Ostionoid, Taino and Carib indigenous culture of the Caribbean from 4,000 BC to 1524 AD. Emphasis on social complexity, religion, art and political organization to illustrate the diversity and richness of Amerindian Caribbean life until their rapid decline after European contact.
ANTH 224.subject: ANTH
ANTH 224.title: Indigenous Caribbean Archaeology

ANTH 225.description: Archaeological images and ideas in modern popular culture, including film and fiction.
ANTH 225.subject: ANTH
ANTH 225.title: Archaeology in Film and Popular Culture

ANTH 226.description: The fundamental elements of human culture as it relates to biblical archaeology. The defining characteristics of different kinds of society through interdependency of language and culture. The affects of modern world interests in defining / redefining this area.
ANTH 226.subject: ANTH
ANTH 226.title: Biblical Archaeology

ANTH 227.description: History and basis of several popular “fringe” ideas about the human past that utilize archaeological information: giants, Ice Age civilizations, and pre-Columbian transoceanic contact.
ANTH 227.subject: ANTH
ANTH 227.title: Forbidden Archaeology: Fantasies, Frauds, and Mysteries of the Human Past

ANTH 228.description: Prehistoric anthropology in North America from the first arrival of man through the beginning of European acculturation.
ANTH 228.subject: ANTH
ANTH 228.title: North American Prehistory

ANTH 229.description: Major cultural milestones and lifeways experienced by Indians in the archeological record of the southeastern U.S., including colonization, religion, trade, invention of pottery, and place-making.
ANTH 229.subject: ANTH
ANTH 229.title: Southeastern Archaeology

ANTH 230.description: Application of techniques and insights of social and cultural anthropology to selected cultural settings in contemporary USA.
ANTH 230.subject: ANTH
ANTH 230.title: Diversity in the United States

ANTH 232.description: Application of the methods techniques of socio-cultural anthropology to the contemporary cultures of SC. Examination of contrasts such as low country and up country, black and white, and rich and poor as they are manifested in cultural patterns.
ANTH 232.subject: ANTH
ANTH 232.title: Contemp Cultures of South Carolina

ANTH 234.description: Ethnographic approach to Caribbean cultures and societies. Topics include colonial histories and experience, gender and race relations, beliefs and religious life, verbal arts, literature, and Creole language.
ANTH 234.subject: ANTH
ANTH 234.title: Caribbean Cultures

ANTH 236.description: A comparative study of ethnographic data on African cultures with emphasis upon its significance for broader anthropological theory.
ANTH 236.subject: ANTH
ANTH 236.title: Cultures of Africa

ANTH 237.description: Diversity of lifestyles and institutions of Islam from Morocco to Indonesia, with attention to everyday life in small communities.
ANTH 237.subject: ANTH
ANTH 237.title: Cultures of Islam

ANTH 238.description: A consideration of selected problems in the social and cultural life of peoples in the Middle East with emphasis on non-Arab populations.
ANTH 238.subject: ANTH
ANTH 238.title: Middle Eastern Cultures

ANTH 240.description: Society and culture in South Asia; economic and political institutions, kinship, and religion as they pertain to the daily lives of people in the Subcontinent. Emphasis on India. Bangladesh, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka also included.
ANTH 240.subject: ANTH
ANTH 240.title: South Asian Cultures

ANTH 241.description: Social and cultural patterns of the region and how they influence current developments, especially Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines.
ANTH 241.subject: ANTH
ANTH 241.title: Southeast Asian Cultures

ANTH 242.description: An overview of Chinese popular culture with an introduction to broad anthropological frameworks concerning popular culture.
ANTH 242.subject: ANTH
ANTH 242.title: Chinese Popular Culture

ANTH 243.description: An exploration of Japanese values and the institutions that shape Japanese behavior through analysis or rural and urban community studies and how Japanese people present themselves.
ANTH 243.subject: ANTH
ANTH 243.title: Japanese Cultures

ANTH 244.description: Contemporary Indian Country in anthropological, historical, cultural, economic, and political contexts.
ANTH 244.subject: ANTH
ANTH 244.title: American Indian Nations Today: From Hard Times to Hard Rock

ANTH 260.description: A survey of field and laboratory investigations of the comparative anatomy and behavior of nonhuman primates.
ANTH 260.subject: ANTH
ANTH 260.title: Planet of the Apes: Behavior and Biology

ANTH 261.description: The biocultural processes of human variation.
ANTH 261.subject: ANTH
ANTH 261.title: Human Variation

ANTH 262.description: Survey of the basic scientific methods and applications of forensic anthropology.
ANTH 262.subject: ANTH
ANTH 262.title: Basic Forensic Anthropology

ANTH 263.description: A cross-disciplinary study of how the bodies of Africans and African Americans were used in medical experimentation, starting in the late 18th century and continuing to the present.
ANTH 263.subject: ANTH
ANTH 263.title: Medical Experimentation and the Black Body

ANTH 270.description: Body language, facial expressions, gestures, use of interpersonal space, and other nonverbal systems of communication and behavior in terms of pertinent theories, research methodology, findings, and cross-cultural implications.
ANTH 270.subject: ANTH
ANTH 270.title: Anthropology of Nonverbal Communication

ANTH 271.description: Linguistic anthropological study of forms of language through the lens of popular culture. Explore the ethnography of communication through play and performance, discursive and semiotic practices, and varieties of language invoked in popular cultural forms that provide resources for cultural reproduction and contestation.
ANTH 271.subject: ANTH
ANTH 271.title: Language and Popular Culture

ANTH 273.description: This course introduces students to the fields of interactional sociolinguistics and linguistic anthropology. Students will learn how they approach the study of cross-cultural and intercultural forms of (mis)communication within the context of globally interconnected people, places, and systems of communication.
ANTH 273.subject: ANTH
ANTH 273.title: Cross-Cultural Communication

ANTH 280.description: Ethnographic study of the Cold War, nuclear culture, and its aftermath.
ANTH 280.subject: ANTH
ANTH 280.title: Humans Going Nuclear: Atomic Bombs, Cold War, and the Fallout

ANTH 287.description: Topics of special interest in archaeology. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 287.subject: ANTH
ANTH 287.title: Special Topics in Archaeology

ANTH 288.description: Topics of special interest in biological anthropology. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 288.subject: ANTH
ANTH 288.title: Special Topics in Biological Anthropology

ANTH 289.description: Topics of special interest in sociocultural anthropology. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 289.subject: ANTH
ANTH 289.title: Special Topics in Sociocultural Anthropology

ANTH 290.description: Topics of special interest in linguistic anthropology. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 290.subject: ANTH
ANTH 290.title: Special Topics in Linguistic Anthropology

ANTH 291.description: Topics of special interest. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 291.subject: ANTH
ANTH 291.title: Selected Topics in Anthropology

ANTH 292.description: Course focuses on political and economic processes contributing to the unequal access to health and social inequalities.
ANTH 292.subject: ANTH
ANTH 292.title: Disease, Health, and Social Inequities

ANTH 301.description: Comparative study of selected Latin American cultures with emphasis on their significance for a broader anthropological theory.
ANTH 301.subject: ANTH
ANTH 301.title: Latin American Cultures

ANTH 303.description: An examination of African-American cultures in the New World.
ANTH 303.subject: ANTH
ANTH 303.title: African-American Cultures

ANTH 313.description: An examination of ethical decision-making encountered in the practice of anthropology.
ANTH 313.subject: ANTH
ANTH 313.title: Ethical Dilemmas in Anthropology

ANTH 318.description: Material aspects of cultures from artifact production in historical societies to contemporary industrial crafts; the cultural context of artifacts; fieldwork; relevant anthropological theories.
ANTH 318.subject: ANTH
ANTH 318.title: Material Culture

ANTH 319.description: Introduction to principles, methods, and theory of archaeology, including prehistoric and historic case studies.
ANTH 319.subject: ANTH
ANTH 319.title: Principles of Archaeology

ANTH 320.description: This course charts the history of ideas in archaeology, over the past century, as a means of understanding current directions in archaeological thinking and current applications in archaeological practice.
ANTH 320.subject: ANTH
ANTH 320.title: Archaeology Theory

ANTH 321.description: Prehistoric and historic archaeology of South Carolina.
ANTH 321.subject: ANTH
ANTH 321.title: South Carolina Archaeology

ANTH 322.description: Archaeological field techniques, laboratory analysis and data interpretation.
ANTH 322.subject: ANTH
ANTH 322.title: Field School in Archaeology

ANTH 323.description: Designing and carrying out ethnographic research including project design, data collection, analysis and description.
ANTH 323.subject: ANTH
ANTH 323.title: Field School in Ethnography

ANTH 324.description: Current research on use of modern material culture in archaeological analysis.
ANTH 324.subject: ANTH
ANTH 324.title: Ethnoarchaeology

ANTH 327.description: Study of Mesoamerican and South American civilizations, particularly the Mayan, Aztec, and Inca states. Processes of state formation as reflected in archaeological data.
ANTH 327.subject: ANTH
ANTH 327.title: Prehistoric Civilizations of the New World

ANTH 328.description: Causes for the rise and fall of several civilizations; ideological and ecological factors, unique events, and personalities versus general processes.
ANTH 328.subject: ANTH
ANTH 328.title: Ancient Civilizations

ANTH 331.description: Cultural development and variation in Mesoamerica from the first arrival of man to the arrival of Europeans. Particular attention to cultural continuities from prehistoric times.
ANTH 331.subject: ANTH
ANTH 331.title: Mesoamerican Prehistory

ANTH 342.subject: ANTH
ANTH 342.title: Environmental Anthropology: Cross-cultural Perspectives on Environmental Change

ANTH 349.description: Techniques, customs, verbal expressions, and expressive styles of workers in a variety of occupational cultures.
ANTH 349.subject: ANTH
ANTH 349.title: Anthropology of Work

ANTH 350.description: An examination of political and economic change in contemporary peasant communities.
ANTH 350.subject: ANTH
ANTH 350.title: Anthropology Development

ANTH 351.description: Kinship, systems of descent, marriage, and domestic organization in different cultures. Variations in childrearing practices, gender, and other aspects of social relations in kin groups.
ANTH 351.subject: ANTH
ANTH 351.title: The Family in Cross-Cultural Perspective

ANTH 353.description: Understanding human behavior through the examination of cultural norms, mechanisms of social control, and social conflict.
ANTH 353.subject: ANTH
ANTH 353.title: Anthropology of Law and Conflict

ANTH 355.description: Language in its social setting. The relationship between linguistic categories and culture categories. Language and cognition.
ANTH 355.subject: ANTH
ANTH 355.title: Language, Culture, and Society

ANTH 356.description: Sculpture, drama, ceramics, weaving, music, and other arts from tribal societies will be discussed in terms of the religious, social, and aesthetic principles that underlie their production, use, and interpretation.
ANTH 356.subject: ANTH
ANTH 356.title: Anthropology of Art

ANTH 357.description: Cultural differences and pan-cultural similarities in such psychological features as personality and cognition.
ANTH 357.subject: ANTH
ANTH 357.title: Psychological Anthropology

ANTH 359.description: Theory and practice of ethnology/sociocultural anthropology, based on a wide range of simple and complex societies.
ANTH 359.subject: ANTH
ANTH 359.title: Theories of Culture

ANTH 360.description: An overview of human sexuality in different cultures in regions across the globe; an examination of anthropological frameworks for sexuality that draws on historical and modern cultural conceptions.
ANTH 360.subject: ANTH
ANTH 360.title: Anthropology of Sex

ANTH 361.description: The processes of homonoid development with a review of the basic principles of physical and behavioral evolution using the fossil record and the evolving ecological and psychosocial contexts.
ANTH 361.subject: ANTH
ANTH 361.title: Becoming Human

ANTH 366.description: An interdisciplinary study of the health of enslaved African Americans during the nineteenth century by focusing on the conceptions, experiences, and dynamics of the relationship between slaves, medicine, healing, and their masters in the Antebellum American South.
ANTH 366.subject: ANTH
ANTH 366.title: Medicine, Disease, and Slavery

ANTH 371.description: Ethnographic analysis of communication in human groups and institutions.
ANTH 371.subject: ANTH
ANTH 371.title: Ethnography of Communication

ANTH 373.description: Introduction to the linguistic component of human cognition. Properties of speech, the organization of language in the mind/brain, cross-linguistic universals, child language acquisition, and aspects of adult language processing.
ANTH 373.subject: ANTH
ANTH 373.title: Introduction to Language Sciences

ANTH 374.description: Bilingual language development, social and cultural aspects of bilingualism, the bilingual brain, bilingualism throughout the lifespan.
ANTH 374.subject: ANTH
ANTH 374.title: Cognitive and Social Aspects of Bilingualism

ANTH 380.description: An in-depth exploration of global health issues through the lens of anthropology with cross-cultural perspectives.
ANTH 380.subject: ANTH
ANTH 380.title: Anthropology of Global Health

ANTH 381.description: Examines the dialectic between globalization and the social construction of gender. Topics include the global assembly line, transnational markets for domestic labor and sex workers, and global feminist alliances.
ANTH 381.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ANTH 102 or WGST 112.
ANTH 381.subject: ANTH
ANTH 381.title: Gender and Globalization

ANTH 388.description: Anthropological study of pregnancy and birth with a cross-cultural focus comparing the United States to other nations. Examination of cultural factors such as prenatal care, dietary practices, taboos, birth location, practitioners, and birthing styles.
ANTH 388.subject: ANTH
ANTH 388.title: Cultures, Pregnancy, and Birth

ANTH 391.description: Topics of special interest. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 391.subject: ANTH
ANTH 391.title: Selected Topics in Anthropology

ANTH 392.description: This course examines health concerns important in the lives of women around the world through an overview of contemporary issues and challenges in the field of global health, broadly construed.
ANTH 392.subject: ANTH
ANTH 392.title: Global Women's Health

ANTH 396.description: An anthropological approach to the study of environmental health, toxicity, and environmental injustice in comparative context.
ANTH 396.subject: ANTH
ANTH 396.title: Toxic Environments and Invisible Harms

ANTH 442.description: Linguistic examination of the structure, history, and use of African-American English, as well as literary presentations, language attitudes, and issues relating to education and the acquisition of Standard English.
ANTH 442.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 101 and ENGL 102, and one course between ENGL 270-ENGL 292.
ANTH 442.subject: ANTH
ANTH 442.title: African-American English

ANTH 497.description: Supervised internship/experiential learning experience relevant to one of the four fields of anthropology.
ANTH 497.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ANTH 102; C or better in ANTH 101 or ANTH 161.
ANTH 497.subject: ANTH
ANTH 497.title: Internship in Anthropology

ANTH 498.description: Directed research resulting in a written report.
ANTH 498.subject: ANTH
ANTH 498.title: Senior Thesis

ANTH 499.description: A seminar synthesizing the major with an examination of anthropology as a field of inquiry.
ANTH 499.subject: ANTH
ANTH 499.title: In the Tradition of Anthropology

ANTH 512.description: Anthropology of gender in Chinese-speaking cultures in Chinese-speaking Asia.
ANTH 512.subject: ANTH
ANTH 512.title: Gender Issues in China

ANTH 513.description: Survey of how each anthropological subfield studies the interrelationships between plants and peoples. Application of methods, including interviewing and data analysis.
ANTH 513.subject: ANTH
ANTH 513.title: Anthropological Ethnobotany

ANTH 515.description: Islam as a dynamic cultural tradition: emphasis on the tension between Islamization and the larger Islamic tradition.
ANTH 515.subject: ANTH
ANTH 515.title: Tradition and Transformations in Islamic Cultures

ANTH 517.description: Cultural representations, constructions, production, and consumption of African-American identity in the popular culture medium of feature films.
ANTH 517.subject: ANTH
ANTH 517.title: An Anthropological View of Blacks in Film

ANTH 518.description: Survey of visual anthropology including theoretical frameworks of ways of seeing, ethnographic photography and filmmaking, contemporary technologies, and their effects on culture.
ANTH 518.subject: ANTH
ANTH 518.title: Visual Cultures

ANTH 520.description: A two-semester class and field session. Research design, field methods, interpretation of data, and the development of theory from the data.
ANTH 520.subject: ANTH
ANTH 520.title: Field Problems in Ethnology

ANTH 525.description: Seminar exploring human-plant-animal-natural interactions within an anthropological framework.
ANTH 525.subject: ANTH
ANTH 525.title: Ethnoecology

ANTH 534.description: Prehistoric archaeology of the South American continent.
ANTH 534.subject: ANTH
ANTH 534.title: Prehistoric Archaeology of South America

ANTH 535.description: Anthropological and archaeological theories and methods in the study of conflict, war, and warfare. Causes, effects, outcomes of sustained social acts of violence of groups, tribes, states, and nations. Evolutionary, biological, social origins of warfare. History, strategy, and tactics, battlefield archaeology.
ANTH 535.subject: ANTH
ANTH 535.title: Conflict Archaeology

ANTH 536.description: Philosophy and mechanics of modern archaeological Cultural Resource Management (CRM). CRM legislation, regulation, and process. Contemporary issues and problems in Public Archaeology including Native American reburial negotiations, conflict resolution, ethics, looting, business practices, standards, contexts and protection.
ANTH 536.subject: ANTH
ANTH 536.title: Public Archaeology

ANTH 541.description: Archaeological field methods and techniques such as excavation, flotation, sampling, surveying, photography, and remote sensing.
ANTH 541.subject: ANTH
ANTH 541.title: Field Problems in Archaeology

ANTH 546.description: Introduction to Forensic Archaeological Recovery (FAR). Concepts, methods, and contemporary issues.
ANTH 546.subject: ANTH
ANTH 546.title: Forensic Archaeological Recovery (FAR)

ANTH 550.description: Laboratory on basic prehistoric and historic artifact analysis, including analytical methods, laboratory equipment, and data interpretation. May be repeated.
ANTH 550.subject: ANTH
ANTH 550.title: Archaeological Laboratory Methods

ANTH 551.description: Application of observation techniques, field notes, informant interviewing, and secondary data analysis to interpreting differential perceptions of health problem solving in the community and clinic.
ANTH 551.subject: ANTH
ANTH 551.title: Medical Anthropology: Fieldwork

ANTH 552.description: Socio-cultural factors in health, illness, healing, and in medical systems. Cross-cultural and ethnographic evidence for public health research and program applications.
ANTH 552.subject: ANTH
ANTH 552.title: Medical Anthropology

ANTH 553.description: The ways people from various cultures reflect on, reinforce, and construct their social realities through narrating, which will be considered as both artistic expression and social action.
ANTH 553.subject: ANTH
ANTH 553.title: Anthropological Approaches to Narrative and Performance

ANTH 555.description: Approaches to gender and language emphasizing the social grounding of both; how language reflects sociocultural values and is a tool for constructing different types of social organization.
ANTH 555.subject: ANTH
ANTH 555.title: Language and Gender

ANTH 556.description: Anthropological approach to issues of language and globalization. Linguistic consequences of globalization under consideration include communicative patterns, linguistic change, and language and political economy.
ANTH 556.subject: ANTH
ANTH 556.title: Language and Globalization

ANTH 557.description: Psychological aspects of behavior from a cross-cultural perspective.
ANTH 557.subject: ANTH
ANTH 557.title: Psychological Anthropology

ANTH 561.description: An intensive examination of the human skeleton and techniques for anthropological interpretation.
ANTH 561.subject: ANTH
ANTH 561.title: Human Osteology

ANTH 565.description: Varieties and effects of disease patterns among past populations illustrating biological, environmental, and cultural interrelationships.
ANTH 565.subject: ANTH
ANTH 565.title: Health and Disease in the Past

ANTH 567.description: Theories and methodologies necessary for the identification of human skeletal remains in a forensic setting.
ANTH 567.subject: ANTH
ANTH 567.title: Human Identification in Forensic Anthropology

ANTH 568.description: Nutritional problems in developing nations. Measures of nutritional status. Social, economic, and environmental aspects of food consumption and nutrition. Biocultural responses to food deprivation and undernutrition.
ANTH 568.subject: ANTH
ANTH 568.title: Nutritional Anthropology

ANTH 569.description: Intersections of international development and environmental change; study of general theoretical perspectives balanced with case studies from the Global South.
ANTH 569.subject: ANTH
ANTH 569.title: International Development and the Environment

ANTH 570.description: Problems in conveying and interpreting ethnographic information on film or tape. Includes syntax, suitability of subject matter to the medium, irrelevant or distracting information, and observer bias.
ANTH 570.subject: ANTH
ANTH 570.title: Ethnographic Film

ANTH 572.description: Clocks, cycles, and contingencies as they affect human societies now and have done so in the past. Theories and models from biology and the other natural sciences will be used to interpret the history of culture.
ANTH 572.subject: ANTH
ANTH 572.title: Temporal Processes in Culture

ANTH 575.description: A cross-cultural study of the economic behavior of pre-literate and literate societies.
ANTH 575.subject: ANTH
ANTH 575.title: Economic Anthropology

ANTH 576.description: Foodways, architecture, crafts, and narrative of African-American cultures.
ANTH 576.subject: ANTH
ANTH 576.title: Archaeology of the African Diaspora

ANTH 577.description: Selected recent theoretical and methodological developments in the study of social organization.
ANTH 577.subject: ANTH
ANTH 577.title: Advanced Topics in the Anthropological Study of Social Organization

ANTH 578.description: Biological, sociocultural, and health-related dimensions of migration, focusing on the movement of people across borders through a biocultural anthropological lens.
ANTH 578.subject: ANTH
ANTH 578.title: Anthropology of Migration: Displacement, Borders, and Health

ANTH 579.description: An interdisciplinary approach to prehistoric, historic, and contemporary relationships between the development of socio-cultural configurations and ecosystems.
ANTH 579.subject: ANTH
ANTH 579.title: Cultural Ecology

ANTH 580.description: Students will explore the African Diaspora as a social, cultural, and historical formation with Africa at its center, focusing on US, Latin American, and Caribbean African-descended communities.
ANTH 580.subject: ANTH
ANTH 580.title: Culture and Identity in the African Diaspora

ANTH 581.description: This course examines cultural understandings of and responses to globalization, examining topics such as its history and theories, migration, economic integration and inequality, identity, social movements, and the environment.
ANTH 581.subject: ANTH
ANTH 581.title: Globalization and Cultural Questions

ANTH 586.description: Anthropological approach to issues of discourse, gender, and emotion. Issues under consideration include the social control, force, and forms of emotional discourse and the relationship between emotion and culture from gender-oriented perspectives.
ANTH 586.subject: ANTH
ANTH 586.title: Discourse, Gender, and Politics of Emotion

ANTH 591.description: Topics of special interest. May be taken more than once as topics change.
ANTH 591.subject: ANTH
ANTH 591.title: Selected Topics

ANTH 600.description: Survey of core areas of linguistics and extensions to closely related disciplines. Introduction to the linguistic component of human cognition. Formal description and analysis of the general properties of speech and language, the organization of language in the mind/brain, and cross-linguistic typology and universals.
ANTH 600.subject: ANTH
ANTH 600.title: Survey of Linguistics

ANTH 701.description: Human origins, human evolution, human prehistory, and cultural existence from its less complex forms to early civilizations. An introduction to the concepts, methods, and data of physical, biological, and archaeological anthropology primarily for teachers. May be taken with, or independently of, ANTH 702 .
ANTH 701.subject: ANTH
ANTH 701.title: Physical Anthropology and Archaeology for Teachers

ANTH 702.description: Selected contemporary cultures, including their languages. An introduction to the concepts, methods, and data of sociocultural anthropology and anthropological linguistics, primarily for teachers. May be taken with, or independently of, ANTH 701 .
ANTH 702.subject: ANTH
ANTH 702.title: Social and Linguistic Anthropology for Teachers

ANTH 703.description: A discussion of the general topics of anthropological inquiry, theories, and methods.
ANTH 703.subject: ANTH
ANTH 703.title: Anthropological Inquiry

ANTH 704.description: Faculty representing subdisciplines of anthropology will explore with students the connections between subfields, theoretical and regional perspectives, and analyses of the past and present.
ANTH 704.subject: ANTH
ANTH 704.title: Anthropological Connections

ANTH 706.description: The origins of global capitalism, the nature of money and debt, the roles of gender, race and class in social formations, and the relationship between production and reproduction.
ANTH 706.subject: ANTH
ANTH 706.title: Engendering Global Capitalism

ANTH 711.description: Presentations of critical skills to achieve career goals in a variety of anthropological applications, develop portfolios, prepare competitive job applications, and produce effective grant proposals. Ethics issues in anthropological research publishing and teaching.
ANTH 711.subject: ANTH
ANTH 711.title: Professionalism and Ethics

ANTH 712.description: Skills needed for writing a master’s thesis in anthropology, including literature review, current theory, research design, data analysis, and written presentation.
ANTH 712.subject: ANTH
ANTH 712.title: Thesis Skills Seminar

ANTH 714.description: Uses the context of leading discussions in ANTH 101 and 102 to introduce and explore issues relating to pedagogy. Restricted to TA's for ANTH 101 and ANTH 102 .

ANTH 714.title: Teaching Practicum in Anthropology
